recommendation: Check for an updated, multi-threaded version of the app; setting its process priority to Below Normal can reduce its impact on the rest of the system.

recommendation: From Recovery > Command Prompt run 'bootrec /rebuildbcd'; if it finds no Windows installations, rebuild manually with 'bcdboot C:\Windows'.

recommendation: Rebuild the boot files from Recovery > Command Prompt with 'bootrec /rebuildbcd' followed by 'bcdboot C:\Windows /s S: /f UEFI' (where S: is the EFI system partition).

recommendation: In an elevated prompt run 'diskpart', 'select disk 1', then 'attributes disk clear readonly'; check for a physical write-protect switch if it's an SD card or USB drive.

summary: The spooler was running but in a stuck state, showing the printer offline. Restarting the Print Spooler cleared the stuck status and the printer returned to Normal.

recommendation: Right-click the app's .exe > Properties > Compatibility > Change high DPI settings > 'Override' and pick 'System (Enhanced)'.

recommendation: Run the update as the SYSTEM context does (no manual elevation fixes this): restore default ACLs with 'icacls C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution /reset /t', temporarily disable third-party antivirus, and retry.

goal: An app fails with error 0x80004005 'Unspecified error' when accessing a network share
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context

Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x80004005 is a catch-all failure, but paired with a network share it almost always maps to an SMB authentication/protocol negotiation failure -- here the client had insecure guest auth disabled while the share only allows guest access.
recommendation: The secure fix is enabling authenticated access on the share (add a real user account on the NAS/server); enabling insecure guest logons on the client works but reintroduces a security risk.

plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context

recommendation: Boot to Recovery and run 'sfc /scannow /offbootdir=C:\ /offwindir=C:\Windows' followed by 'DISM /Image:C:\ /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'; if a third-party credential/logon tool was recently installed, uninstall it from Safe Mode.

summary: 0x80070490 indicates a corrupted entry in the component-based servicing (CBS) store or a damaged system file the update depends on -- the update engine literally can't find a manifest element it expects.
recommendation: Run DISM RestoreHealth then SFC (in that order), reboot, and retry the update; if it still fails, install the update manually from the Microsoft Update Catalog.

goal: MSI installer fails with error 1603 'A fatal error occurred during installation'

recommendation: Re-run with verbose logging ('msiexec /i app.msi /L*v log.txt') to confirm the failing action, clear the target folder's lock/permission problem, ensure no other MSI is in progress, and retry.

goal: Enabling .NET Framework 3.5 fails with error 0x800F081F 'source files could not be found'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x800F081F means the on-demand feature payload isn't in the local component store and Windows couldn't fetch it (commonly blocked by WSUS policy that redirects feature-on-demand requests away from Windows Update).
recommendation: Enable it with an explicit source from matching install media: 'DISM /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:NetFx3 /All /Source:D:\sources\sxs /LimitAccess', or have IT enable the 'Specify settings for optional component installation' GPO to allow direct Windows Update fetch.

goal: Windows 10 to 11 feature update fails with 0xC1900101 and rolls back

recommendation: Update or temporarily uninstall the specific driver/security product named in setuperr.log, disconnect nonessential peripherals, and retry the feature update; reinstall the software afterward.

goal: Installing from a USB/ISO fails with error 0x80070570 'The file or directory is corrupted and unreadable'

recommendation: Re-download the ISO and re-create the USB with the official Media Creation Tool; if a verified-good USB still throws 0x80070570, run MemTest86 because failing RAM produces this same error.

recommendation: Stop wuauserv/bits/cryptsvc, rename both 'SoftwareDistribution' and 'System32\catroot2', restart the services, and re-check for updates so everything re-downloads cleanly.

recommendation: Report to IT: the WsusPool IIS application pool on the WSUS server needs restarting (and usually a private-memory limit increase to stop it recycling under load).

recommendation: Update or uninstall the software owning the faulting DLL (screen-overlay/RGB/antivirus injectors are common); if unclear, run the app with overlays disabled to confirm.

recommendation: Update the Wi-Fi adapter driver (the usual culprit for 0x9F on laptops), and as a stopgap disable 'Allow the computer to turn off this device' on that adapter so suspend doesn't hang on it.

recommendation: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic/MemTest86; set both DIMMs to the same (lower) speed in BIOS or replace the mismatched kit with a matched pair.

recommendation: Start W32Time and resync ('Start-Service W32Time; w32tm /resync'); with a correct clock the TLS errors disappear. If the clock drifts again after shutdowns, replace the CMOS battery.

recommendation: Report to IT that port 1688 to the KMS host is blocked from this subnet (or the KMS host is down); once reachable, activate immediately with 'slmgr /ato'.

goal: Service operations fail with 0x800706BA 'The RPC server is unavailable' against a remote machine

recommendation: Enable the 'Remote Service Management' / 'Windows Management Instrumentation' firewall rule groups on the remote host (or the equivalent GPO), which open TCP 135 plus the dynamic RPC range.

recommendation: On the target machine, enable 'File and Printer Sharing' in the firewall for the correct network profile, and confirm the 'Server' (LanmanServer) service is running.

goal: Windows installation fails with 0x80300024 'Windows is unable to install to the selected location'

recommendation: Patch the unpatched side (preferred) with current Windows updates; only as a temporary bridge, relax enforcement via the 'Encryption Oracle Remediation' GPO, and revert once both sides are patched.

recommendation: Stop WSearch, delete the search Data folder contents so the index rebuilds from scratch, restart the service, and exclude the search database path from cleanup tools.

recommendation: Replace mapped drive letters with full UNC paths in the script, and set the task's 'Start in' directory explicitly; grant the run-as account NTFS access to the UNC target.

goal: Printing fails with error 0x0000011B on a shared network printer

recommendation: Update both client and print server fully with current Windows updates, then remove and re-add the printer connection; avoid registry workarounds that disable RPC authentication hardening.

goal: Windows Backup (wbadmin) fails with 0x8078002A on a large external drive
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context

Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: 0x8078002A occurs when block-level backup hits a target using 4K-native sectors that the backup engine can't handle -- the external drive reports 4096-byte logical sectors, which wbadmin's VHD format doesn't support.
recommendation: Use a 512-byte-emulation (512e) drive as the backup target, check the drive vendor's tool for a sector-emulation mode, or switch to File History/a third-party imaging tool that supports 4Kn targets.

goal: Domain join fails with error 0x6D9 'There are no more endpoints available from the endpoint mapper'
plan: Identify what the specific error code means in this context
Confirm the root cause with read-only checks
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

summary: The Master File Table has damaged records; chkdsk's read-only scan reports unreadable MFT segments, meaning metadata for some files is lost even though their data clusters may be intact.

goal: USN Journal corruption breaks backup/sync tools with 'The USN journal is invalid' errors

recommendation: Delete and recreate the journal: 'fsutil usn deletejournal /d D:' then 'fsutil usn createjournal m=32768000 a=4096000 D:'; affected tools will do one full rescan and then resume incremental tracking.

goal: A file shows 0 bytes in Explorer but takes real disk space -- data hidden in Alternate Data Streams
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The file's content lives in a named NTFS alternate data stream rather than the main stream, so Explorer shows zero size; ADS is legitimate NTFS functionality but also a classic data-hiding spot.
recommendation: Read the stream with 'Get-Content note.txt -Stream hidden' to inspect it; remove with 'Remove-Item note.txt -Stream hidden'. Audit unexpected ADS on user-writable paths -- malware droppers use them for staging.

goal: A backup tool loops forever on a folder tree -- a junction points back into its own parent
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.command: Get-ChildItem C:\Data -Recurse -Attributes ReparsePoint -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object FullName, Target

summary: A directory junction inside the tree targets an ancestor folder, creating an infinite recursion loop for any tool that follows reparse points instead of detecting cycles.
recommendation: Remove the looping junction ('Remove-Item C:\Data\Archive\Loop' removes only the link, not the target), and configure backup tools to not follow reparse points, which also protects against future loops.

goal: Hard-linked files confuse disk usage tools -- deleting a 'copy' doesn't free space
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The files are hard links: multiple directory entries sharing one data extent, so space frees only when the last link is deleted -- usage tools double-count them and deletions of one name appear to 'do nothing'.
recommendation: This is expected NTFS behavior (used heavily by WinSxS); to actually reclaim space, all link names must be removed. Use tools that count hard links once when auditing usage.

goal: Disk quota exceeded errors for a user even though the volume has plenty of free space

Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

Quota state: Enforced
User: CORP\jdoe  Limit: 10 GB  Used: 10.4 GB

summary: Per-user NTFS quotas are enforced on this volume, and the user's charged bytes (including files they own anywhere on the volume) exceed their limit -- overall free space is irrelevant to the quota check.
recommendation: Raise or remove the user's quota entry ('fsutil quota modify' or the volume's Quota tab), or have the user delete/transfer ownership of large files; quota charges follow file ownership, not folder location.

goal: ACL corruption -- Explorer's Security tab shows 'The permissions on ... are incorrectly ordered' errors
plan: Diagnose the ntfs issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: D:\Share\Projects: The ACL is not in canonical form.

summary: The security descriptor's ACEs are stored in non-canonical order (explicit denies must precede allows, etc.), typically after a nonconforming tool wrote the ACL directly -- Windows refuses edits until order is fixed.
recommendation: Fix with 'icacls D:\Share\Projects /reset /t' (rebuilds from inheritance) if inherited permissions suffice, or reorder in the Security tab's Advanced dialog by re-applying permissions; identify and stop the tool writing broken ACLs.

goal: SMB signing mismatch -- connecting to a hardened server fails with 'The cryptographic signature is invalid'
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The server now requires SMB signing per new policy, and this client has signing disabled via an old registry tweak, so the security negotiation fails outright rather than falling back.
recommendation: Re-enable client signing: 'Set-SmbClientConfiguration -EnableSecuritySignature $true' (and remove the legacy registry tweak that disabled it); signing adds minimal overhead on modern hardware.

goal: Offline Files (Client-Side Caching) shows stale content and won't sync back to the server
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The Offline Files cache database is stuck in a conflicted state; the sync center reports conflicts but the CSC cache itself is damaged, so resolution attempts loop without writing changes server-side.
recommendation: Save copies of locally changed files first, then reinitialize the CSC cache (set HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CSC\Parameters\FormatDatabase=1 and reboot) -- this discards the cache and re-syncs cleanly from the server.

goal: Network discovery shows no computers in File Explorer's Network view though shares work by UNC path
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Discovery depends on the Function Discovery services and the network profile being Private; here the profile is Public (which disables discovery by design) after the last network change.
recommendation: Set the network to Private ('Set-NetConnectionProfile -Name HomeLAN -NetworkCategory Private') and ensure Function Discovery Resource Publication / FDPHost services run; UNC paths bypass discovery, which is why they still worked.

goal: Share permissions vs NTFS permissions mismatch -- user has Full Control on the share but still can't write
plan: Diagnose the smb issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Effective access over SMB is the most restrictive combination of share and NTFS permissions: the share grants Full Control but NTFS grants only Read, so writes fail despite the generous share ACL.
recommendation: Grant the group Modify at the NTFS level ('icacls D:\Shares\TeamDocs /grant "CORP\team-users:(OI)(CI)M"'); best practice is Everyone/Authenticated Users Full at the share layer and real control via NTFS.

goal: Two machines report SID-related trust errors after being cloned from the same image without sysprep
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: (identical UUID/SID lineage confirmed across both clones)

summary: Both clones share the same machine SID and, more critically, identical computer account credentials history -- domain trust and some security functions misbehave because the clones were never generalized with sysprep.
recommendation: Rebuild the clones properly: run 'sysprep /generalize' on the source image and redeploy; for the existing machines, disjoin, delete their AD computer objects, and rejoin after re-generalizing.

goal: Kerberos fails for one service with 'duplicate SPN' errors and intermittent authentication
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks

Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

Found 1 group of duplicate SPNs:
HTTP/intranet.corp.local registered on CORP\svc-web-old and CORP\svc-web

summary: The same ServicePrincipalName is registered on two different accounts, so the KDC issues tickets for whichever it finds first -- when it's the wrong account, the service can't decrypt the ticket and auth fails intermittently.
recommendation: Remove the SPN from the obsolete account ('setspn -D HTTP/intranet.corp.local svc-web-old'); duplicate SPNs must never coexist -- the intermittent pattern matches which object the KDC happened to resolve.

goal: Applications fail LDAP binds against the Global Catalog while normal LDAP (389) works
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The app queries the Global Catalog on port 3268, and the only local GC-enabled DC is offline -- regular LDAP on 389 still answers from a non-GC DC, which is why only GC-dependent lookups fail.
recommendation: Bring the GC DC back online or enable the GC role on another local DC (NTDS Settings > Global Catalog checkbox), then allow replication to complete; site designs should always include at least two GCs.

goal: A branch office Read-Only Domain Controller (RODC) can't authenticate some users when the WAN is down
plan: Diagnose the activedirectory issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The RODC only caches passwords for accounts in its Password Replication Policy allow list; users outside it require a writable DC over the WAN, so they fail exactly when the WAN link is down.
recommendation: Add the branch users' group to the RODC's allowed Password Replication Policy and pre-populate their secrets ('repadmin /rodcpwdrepl'); only cached accounts survive WAN outages by design.

goal: Reverse DNS lookups fail (PTR records missing) breaking tools that resolve IPs to names
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Resolve-DnsName : DNS name does not exist

summary: The forward zone is healthy but no reverse lookup zone exists for the subnet, so PTR queries have nowhere to land -- reverse zones are never created automatically.
recommendation: Create the reverse zone (2.0.10.in-addr.arpa) on the DNS server, enable secure dynamic updates so clients register their own PTRs, and add static PTRs for servers/printers with static IPs.

goal: Stale DNS records accumulate -- offline machines still resolve because scavenging never runs
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Aging/scavenging is disabled on the zone, so dynamically registered records persist forever after machines are gone; lookups keep resolving to dead IPs.
recommendation: Enable aging on the zone and scavenging on the server ('Set-DnsServerZoneAging corp.local -Aging $true' plus Set-DnsServerScavenging with sensible no-refresh/refresh intervals matched to DHCP lease duration); verify timestamps before first scavenge so valid records aren't purged.

goal: Domain controller SRV records missing from DNS -- clients can't locate DCs after a DNS rebuild
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Resolve-DnsName : DNS name does not exist

summary: The _ldap/_kerberos SRV records under _msdcs were lost in the zone rebuild, and clients discover DCs exclusively through them -- without SRVs, domain operations fail even though A records exist.
recommendation: On each DC, restart the Netlogon service ('Restart-Service Netlogon') which re-registers all its SRV records automatically; verify with the same SRV query, and check the zone allows secure dynamic updates.

goal: Secondary DNS server's zone is stale -- zone transfers (AXFR/IXFR) are being refused
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The primary's zone-transfer settings don't include the new secondary's IP, so transfer requests are refused and the secondary keeps serving its aging copy until expiry.
recommendation: Add the new secondary's IP to the allowed transfer list ('Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone corp.local -SecondaryServers 10.0.1.10,10.0.1.11 -SecureSecondaries TransferToSecureServers') and trigger a transfer from the secondary.

goal: DNSSEC validation failures -- some external domains fail with SERVFAIL only through the internal resolver
plan: Diagnose the dns-advanced issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The internal resolver has DNSSEC validation enabled and its trust anchor for the root zone is outdated (missed the KSK rollover), so signed domains fail validation while unsigned ones resolve fine.
recommendation: Update the root trust anchor to the current KSK ('Add-DnsServerTrustAnchor -Root' after enabling automatic RFC 5011 rollover support), then clear the resolver cache; keep automatic trust-anchor updates on.

goal: PXE boot fails -- clients don't receive boot server info though DHCP addressing works
plan: Diagnose the dhcp issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: DHCP options 66 (boot server) and 67 (boot file name) aren't set on the scope, so PXE clients get an IP but no next-server/boot path -- addressing and PXE bootstrap are separate option sets.
recommendation: Set option 66 to the WDS/SCCM PXE server's FQDN and 67 to the boot file (e.g., smsboot\x64\wdsmgfw.efi for UEFI) -- or better, configure IP helpers on routers to forward PXE broadcasts natively, which handles BIOS/UEFI differences more reliably than static options.

goal: DHCP failover partners show different lease data -- clients get NAKs when the partner answers
plan: Diagnose the dhcp issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The failover relationship is out of sync (partner state COMMUNICATION_INTERRUPTED); each server holds divergent lease tables, so a renewal answered by the wrong partner produces a NAK.
recommendation: Restore connectivity between the DHCP partners (port 647 TCP), then resynchronize the relationship ('Invoke-DhcpServerv4FailoverReplication'); investigate what broke the partner channel -- often a firewall change.

goal: Users intermittently get addresses from an unauthorized (rogue) DHCP server on the LAN

Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

steps.stdout: Lease obtained from server 192.168.0.1 (not the corporate 10.0.0.10)

recommendation: Locate and remove the rogue device (trace the offending server's MAC via switch tables), and enable DHCP snooping on managed switches so only authorized ports may answer DHCP -- the durable fix against repeats.

recommendation: Stop/reconfigure the conflicting process (or remove its stale reservation with 'netsh http delete urlacl'), then start the IIS site; two listeners can't own the same IP:port:host combination in HTTP.sys.

plan: Diagnose the iis issue with read-only checks

recommendation: Configure HSTS at the site level (IIS 10.0+ has native HSTS settings on the site's HSTS dialog; enable includeSubDomains and an appropriate max-age), and keep exactly one canonical HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect rule.

goal: Certificate auto-enrollment silently stopped -- machine certs expire without renewal

Identify the specific root cause

recommendation: Restore Enroll + Autoenroll permissions for the computers' group on the certificate template (Certification Authority console > template Security tab), then 'certutil -pulse' on clients to trigger immediate re-enrollment.

goal: L2TP/IPsec VPN fails behind home routers with error 809 -- no response from server
plan: Diagnose the vpn issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: Error 809 means the IPsec negotiation packets never made it through: the NAT router isn't passing ESP/UDP 4500 properly, and Windows by default won't attempt IPsec over double-NAT without the NAT-T registry setting.
recommendation: Set AssumeUDPEncapsulationContextOnSendRule=2 under PolicyAgent and reboot (enables NAT-T through double NAT), confirm UDP 500/4500 pass the router, and prefer IKEv2/SSTP where possible -- they traverse NAT far better.

goal: SSTP VPN fails with error 0x80092013 'The revocation function was unable to check revocation'
plan: Diagnose the vpn issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

recommendation: Publish the CRL on an internet-reachable endpoint (standard practice for SSTP deployments); as a stopgap only, clients can set NoCertRevocationCheck=1 for SSTP -- but fixing CRL reachability is the correct solution.

goal: IKEv2 VPN connects but no traffic flows -- small packets work, large transfers stall (MTU blackhole)

Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation

recommendation: Lower the VPN interface MTU to the discovered working size ('netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "VPN" mtu=1350 store=persistent'), and/or enable MSS clamping on the VPN server so all TCP flows self-adjust.

goal: Always On VPN user tunnel never auto-connects for some users after deployment

goal: Wi-Fi drops every time weather radar is nearby -- 5 GHz DFS channel interruptions

recommendation: Configure the AP to prefer non-DFS channels (36-48, 149-165 where permitted) if drops are frequent at this location; DFS channels offer cleaner spectrum but carry mandatory radar-vacate behavior.

goal: A device can't join Wi-Fi -- MAC filtering blocks it because MAC randomization gives a new address

recommendation: Either disable random hardware addresses for this network (Wi-Fi network Properties toggle) and whitelist the true MAC, or preferably drop MAC filtering entirely -- it adds admin burden with negligible security value.

goal: Hyper-V Live Migration fails with 'The credentials supplied to the package were not recognized' between two hosts

recommendation: Add matching constrained delegation entries (use Kerberos-only) on both host computer accounts for each other's migration and cifs services, or switch migration authentication to CredSSP (requires initiating from a console session).

recommendation: Free or add space on the volume (move another VM's files off temporarily), then delete the checkpoint so the merge can complete; adopt a policy of removing checkpoints within days -- they're not backups.

recommendation: Attach the disk to a Generation 2 VM (matching its UEFI/GPT layout), or convert the OS image to MBR/BIOS boot with MBR2GPT-in-reverse tooling/reinstall if Gen1 is truly required (legacy OSes only).

goal: docker compose up fails with 'network ... overlaps with other one on this address space'

recommendation: Set a non-conflicting address pool in Docker's daemon settings ('default-address-pools' e.g. 10.200.0.0/16) and explicit subnets in compose networks; pick ranges the VPN never routes.

goal: Switching between Windows containers and Linux containers breaks builds with 'no matching manifest for windows/amd64'
plan: Diagnose the docker issue with read-only checks
Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
summary: The daemon is in Windows-containers mode while the compose/build references Linux-only images; each mode can only run its own OS's images, and the error is the registry saying no Windows variant exists for that image.
recommendation: Switch Docker Desktop back to Linux containers mode for Linux images (or use '--platform linux/amd64' with WSL2 backend which runs both via integration); keep separate compose files if genuinely mixing Windows and Linux workloads.

goal: WSL2 DNS resolution fails inside distros while Windows resolves fine

Identify the specific root cause
Apply the appropriate fix or escalation
